reason: I opened the cited AUS news page (dated 6 November 2025) and it states every factual element of the claim: first place went to team Hayyakum of AUS (Mahmoud Darwish, Amr Mohi Aldeen, Mohamad Dabbagh, Afif Zughayer) for "Sharjah Quest", described as "a gamified tourism application through which visitors collect digital stamps, unlock mascots and follow curated itineraries"; the team's own description calls it an "augmented reality-powered mobile adventure" with a digital passport, heritage mascots, citywide challenges, quests, stamps, badges, and leaderboards across museums, souqs, heritage houses, natural sites, and local SMEs, plus real-time guidance; "The team earned AED 20,000 and will present their solution at SITTF 2025." The hackathon ran 1 to 2 November 2025 as part of SITTF 2025. An independent government-affiliated report on Sharjah24 (6 November 2025) repeats all of the same details, and the Ajman University news page independently confirms the event name, dates, organizers, and third place. A Sharjah24 article of 19 November 2025 confirms SITTF 2025 took place and lists the hackathon among its new features, though it does not describe the winner's presentation itself. Two precision points: (1) the sources describe an AR-powered app with real-time guidance and curated itineraries, not an "AR guide" as such (the "virtual tour guide" wording belongs to the third-place project trail/s), so "AR layer, itinerary and real-time guidance, and gamification" is the more accurate reading; (2) the stage slot is reported prospectively ("will present"), and no opened source confirms the presentation happened. The second half of the claim (overlap with "their draft") could not be checked against the draft: D:\Sharjah Tourism Hackathon holds only 00_Hackathon_Brief.md and 03_AI_Usage_Disclosure.md, neither of which describes a treasure hunt, AR guide, or route planning; the scratchpad holds only organizer documents and a journal article; and no artifact in the user's list is a Sharjah draft (TwinPath is an unrelated landing-page study). What the sources do establish is that Sharjah Quest covers an AR layer, itineraries with guidance, and gamification, so a draft containing those three features would overlap on all three, not only on a treasure-hunt mechanic. Side note worth passing on: two Hayyakum members, Afif Zughayer and Mahmoud Darwish, appear as mentors in the 2026 brief (00_Hackathon_Brief.md section 7).
corrected_claim: The 2025 Sharjah Tourism Innovation Hackathon (1 to 2 November 2025, AUS, held as part of SITTF 2025) was won by team Hayyakum (AUS: Mahmoud Darwish, Amr Mohi Aldeen, Mohamad Dabbagh, Afif Zughayer) with Sharjah Quest, an augmented reality-powered gamified tourism app in which visitors use a digital passport to collect digital stamps, unlock heritage mascots, follow curated itineraries with real-time guidance, and complete quests for badges and leaderboard rankings across museums, souqs, heritage houses, natural sites, and local small and medium-sized enterprises. The team earned AED 20,000 and was to present the solution at SITTF 2025. Sharjah Quest therefore spans an AR layer, itinerary and guidance, and gamification, not only a treasure-hunt mechanic. Source: https://www.aus.edu/media/news/sharjah-tourism-innovation-hackathon-at-aus-reimagines-travel-and-tourism-experience (independent confirmation: https://sharjah24.ae/en/Articles/2025/11/06/Innovation-Hackathon-reimagines-tourism-experience-at-AUS)
